title: Playbook pressure-test + roleplay (Field Reps)
summary: Internal enablement session to pressure-test new playbook messaging and run two live roleplays: one enterprise CTO objection (latency/cost/private deployment) and one procurement pricing negotiation. Practiced rebuttals, clarified security talking points (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and agreed next steps to update battlecards and schedule 1:1 coaching.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment
Demo cadence and live prompt examples
action_items: Sofia Patel - update playbook slides with new latency vs cost chart - due 2025-10-18
Marcus Li - record a 6-min demo clip showing canary fallback behavior - due 2025-10-15
Renee Cho - publish revised battlecard and share on internal channel - due 2025-10-17
next_steps: Sofia to send updated playbook deck + sample prompts
Schedule 1:1 roleplay with top 5 field reps by 2025-10-20
Collect top 10 customer objections from week of 2025-10-13 and iterate on rebuttals
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (AE), Marcus (SE), Renee (CSM), Jenna (Field Rep), Omar (Field Rep), Luca (Intern)

---
00:00 Sofia: ok, hi everyone, thanks for making the time. we'll do a quick 10-12 minute walkthrough of the new playbook then run two roleplays. marcus is gonna flag technical quick hits, renee will note coaching points. sound good?
00:18 Jenna: yep, sounds great. thanks, so excited to practice.
00:22 Marcus: quick note, i'll call out one demo snippet on canary fallbacks and then a KV cache example where people tend to trip up.
00:33 Sofia: perfect. so first, the messaging thesis: we lean into production economics — not just model quality — latency, cost, and predictable capacity. short phrase: "serve, not own".
00:52 Omar: can you repeat that line? i forget the exact wording when i'm nervous.
00:56 Sofia: yeah: "We help you ship reliable LLM features with predictable latency and unit economics — so you can focus on product, not model ops." little long, but you can tighten it.
01:12 Luca: do we lead with cost or latency? some of our reps start with cost and the customer says, 'ok but what's the quality tradeoff'
01:20 Sofia: good, great Q. we zone by persona — for infra/platform buyer lead with latency and SLAs; for product/ops lead with unit economics and SLOs. both tie back to our auto-fallbacks and dedicated options.
01:36 Marcus: technically, highlight KV cache and batching benefits on throughput slides — those are real dollar-savers versus naive endpoints. say something like: "Automatic KV caching reduces repeated prefix compute, dropping per-token compute by up to X% in many chat workloads". (note: X is illustrative in playbook).
01:56 Jenna: nice. okay roleplay 1: i'll be CTO of FinServ App Inc who cares about PII and residency. go.
02:04 Sofia: hi, jenna, thanks for taking the time. quick question — what's top of mind for the project?
02:10 Jenna (CTO persona): two things: latency — customers are latency sensitive for realtime support — and security: we need on-prem for PCI and strong KMS controls. also, who owns the tokens and logs?
02:22 Sofia: totally fair. shortest pitch: we have three deployment modes. Hosted for fast time to value, Dedicated for isolated GPU pools with predictable throughput and SLA, and Private for full VPC/on-prem control when regulated workloads require it. for KMS, we support customer-managed keys and integrate with common HSMs.
02:40 Marcus: (interject) for the private option, we have audit log hooks that can stream to customer SIEMs and we map RBAC to SSO. if they ask latency, mention that private can actually reduce cross-region hops — so it's often lowest-latency for regional workloads.
03:02 Jenna (CTO): hmm, sounds good, what about unit cost? private seems expensive. the procurement team will push back.
03:08 Sofia: yes, acknowledge cost. say: "Dedicated and Private give you predictability and compliance; we help control cost through batching, quantization recommendations, and autoscaling policies." then offer a pilot to baseline their QPS and show unit economics.
03:26 Jenna (CTO): can you commit to a performance number?
03:29 Marcus: we avoid hard SLOs in discovery — say roughs: 50–100ms for short prompts on our lowest-latency hosted model, realistic depends on sequence length and model family. for enterprise we'll run a short benchmark with your sample prompts and report back with P50/P95.
03:47 Sofia: and cap it: "we'll run a targeted benchmark during pilot and share a report with latency and cost levers".
03:55 Omar: side note — how often do we talk about quantization? some reps avoid it cause it sounds 'fuzzy'.
04:00 Marcus: say: "we offer quantization recommendations that usually reduce GPU memory and cost with minimal quality impact for many workloads — we'll A/B test it during pilot". keep it concrete.

04:18 Roleplay debrief:
04:20 Renee: good use of pilot as safe path. one coaching tip: don't oversell the numbers. instead promise a benchmark and deliver. call out you should capture the sample prompt set during discovery.

04:40 Sofia: ok, second roleplay — procurement/pricing negotiation. jenna will now be procurement. ready?
04:46 Jenna (procurement persona): yes. i need a 30% reduction on list to push the deal internal. also concerned about hidden token fees and support costs.
04:55 Sofia: i hear you. reply: "we price transparently per token and for Dedicated we have committed capacity discounts. common levers are term commitments and consumption buffers — let's map expected QPS to a committed plan and we can show you modeled spend with and without caching."
05:12 Jenna (procurement): and support — enterprise support seems pricey. can you include a 24/7 hotline?
05:18 Renee: three ways: include support in the contract for initial term, offer cheaper SLA tiers for lower-cost bundles, or include a short-term pilot support package at no additional cost. give options.
05:30 Jenna (procurement): ok i'll ask for included pilot support and a two-quarter term reduction.

05:40 Marcus: demo point — when you do live pricing conversations, open the cost model spreadsheet and walk one line: QPS -> tokens/request -> monthly tokens -> unit price -> discount for committed capacity. simple and repeatable.
05:58 Sofia: great. now quick technical objection that trips reps: 'what if fallback model quality is lower?'
06:06 Marcus: say: "we orchestrate model variants with automatic fallback and quality monitoring; fallbacks are vetted for the specific prompt families in your evals and we tie regressions to alerts". mention rollouts/canary.
06:20 Jenna: sometimes the customer asks about 'retraining' or 'model editing' — how do we respond?
06:25 Sofia: for product teams: "We recommend prompt engineering, few-shot examples, and eval sets first; model version pinning and controlled rollouts reduce regressions. retraining is customer-managed or via partner engagements". keep it directional.

06:45 Technical micro-demo (Marcus): 
06:47 Marcus: (walkthrough) ok, open the console slide — here's per-route latency histogram, token-level cost breakdown, and a canary rollout example. you can show the tracing link to grab a slow request and then show KV cache hits reducing tokens.
07:10 Jenna: oh that trace UI — some reps fumble the nav. any one-liner to find it quickly?
07:14 Marcus: yes: top nav -> Observability -> Requests -> filter by route name -> click trace id. tell reps to have a saved bookmark for the common debug dashboard.
07:26 Luca: quick question: in the deck we say 'prefix caching' — will customers know what that is?
07:30 Sofia: maybe rephrase to 'context caching (KV cache)' and add a one-liner: 'stores repeated conversation prefixes to avoid recomputing the same tokens'

07:45 Mid-meeting check:
07:47 Renee: we're at about 20 minutes, let's speed to the second demo clip and the final 15 minutes of Q&A roleplay.
07:54 Sofia: ok next live snippet: canary fallback.
08:00 Marcus: (demo narration) we flip a canary on 10% of traffic to a tuned Llama-variant and monitor latency and hallucination rates. if regression > threshold we auto-failover. emphasize 'automatic fallback' — it's a reliability story.
08:22 Jenna: customers ask what 'hallucination metric' is — is there a standard measure we use?
08:27 Marcus: we use custom evals and a simple mismatch rate on labelled outputs (precision-style). don't go deep — say 'we track quality with prompt-specific evals and alert on regressions'.

08:40 Roleplay 3 (rapid-fire objections)
08:42 Omar: i'll rapid-fire: 'we can't store data in your cloud', 'what about latency spikes', 'how do you integrate with SSO', 'who do i call during incident'
08:50 Sofia: quick replies: for storage: private/VPC or dedicated; latency spikes: autoscaling + fallback; SSO: SAML/SCIM supported; incident: enterprise support contact and on-call rotation.
09:10 Jenna: sometimes reps overcommit on 'we do everything' — callout?
09:14 Renee: always hedge with 'we'll validate in pilot and show results'. use pilot as the optical closure.

09:30 Final coaching tips:
09:32 Sofia: 1) capture sample prompts early; 2) use pilot as measurement; 3) avoid exact performance numbers until benchmark; 4) close for a pilot with a clear success criteria (latency target, cost per request, integration milestone).
09:55 Marcus: tech tip: when they ask about 'KV cache size' or 'quantization level', redirect to 'we'll recommend config after seeing workload' — i.e., don't guess memory numbers.
10:10 Jenna: ok, that felt good. small ask — can we add a cheat-sheet with exact phrasing for the three deployment modes?
10:17 Sofia: yes, action: i'll add a one-pager. renee will distribute.
10:23 Renee: i'll also record the key roleplay transcripts and post highlights.
10:30 Quick open Q&A from field reps:
10:32 Luca: for the price sheet, what's the typical discount corridor for a mid-market ARR 500k deal?
10:37 Sofia: say 10-25% off list depending on term and committed capacity. frame it as negotiable and tied to usage guarantees.
10:46 Omar: when customers ask for on-prem, do we have an 'air-gapped' reference?
10:50 Marcus: yes mention our private deployment offering; there is an on-prem package for large regulated customers — reference architecture exists but redirect to Solutions Eng for scoping.
11:05 Final recap and close:
11:06 Sofia: recap: we'll update the playbook with cheat-sheet and latency-cost chart, marcus will record demo clips, renee will publish battlecards, and we'll schedule 1:1 roleplays. thanks everyone — great energy.
11:22 Jenna: thanks, super helpful.
11:25 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript: occasional filler words and small transcription errors present (e.g., 'K-V cache' occasionally written with dashes, 'Red-wood' heard in one snippet). Some timestamps approximate.
